title: The Batman and the Bridge Builder

sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: We talk to a lot of architects on the show, but this week, we're talking to an engineer.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中采访过很多建筑师，但本周我们要采访一位工程师。

sentences.en: My name is Mark Blaschok, and I am a professional engineer in the state of Texas.
sentences.zh: 我叫马克·布拉斯乔克，我是德克萨斯州的注册专业工程师。
他就像是，真的是德州人？

sentences.en: I'm a fourth or fifth generation Texan.
sentences.zh: 我是第四代或第五代德州人。
我都忘了到底是第几代了。

sentences.en: But I've been raised in other parts of the country, too.
sentences.zh: 但我也是在国家其他地方长大的。

sentences.en: So I can talk to talk because I have been raised in the East Coast, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以我很能聊得来，因为我在东海岸长大的，你知道的。

sentences.en: We talked to Mark about one of the first projects that he ever worked on.
sentences.zh: 我们跟马克聊了他最早参与的项目之一。
那是制片人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: He had just graduated from college at the University of Houston,
sentences.zh: 他刚从休斯顿大学毕业不久，

sentences.en: and he'd gotten a job in Austin with the Texas Department of Transportation.
sentences.zh: 并在奥斯汀的德克萨斯州交通运输局找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: I was in my mid-20s at the time, so 40 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我当时二十多岁，那是40年前的事了。

sentences.en: Well, actually, I like to say four decades.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上，我喜欢说四十年。

sentences.en: And I was assigned to a number of things, but I ended up on the Congress Avenue Bridge.
sentences.zh: 我被分配做了很多事情，但最终落脚在国会大道桥上。

sentences.en: That is the reconstruction of the Congress Avenue Bridge.
sentences.zh: 也就是国会大道桥的重建工程。

sentences.en: The Ann Richards Congress Avenue Bridge is just a simple concrete arch bridge
sentences.zh: 安·理查兹国会大道桥是一座简单的混凝土拱桥，

sentences.en: that spans Lady Bird Lake in downtown Austin.
sentences.zh: 横跨奥斯汀市中心的伯德夫人湖。

sentences.en: The bridge was completed in 1910, but by the late 1970s, it was in need of a tune-up.
sentences.zh: 这座桥于1910年建成，但到了20世纪70年代末，它需要整修了。

sentences.en: It was structurally deficient, and so it was rebuilt.
sentences.zh: 它的结构不符合标准，所以进行了重建。

sentences.en: And more conventional, more modern, more contemporary beams were put in called box beaMs.
sentences.zh: 并且安装了更常规、更现代、更当代的梁，被称为箱梁。

sentences.en: The box beams sit below the road's surface, and they need to be spaced a certain distance apart.
sentences.zh: 箱梁位于路面下方，它们需要保持一定的间距。

sentences.en: Mark and the other engineers decided that the gap should be somewhere between three-quarters of an inch and an inch and a half.
sentences.zh: 马克和其他工程师决定，这个间隙应该在四分之三英寸到一英寸半之间。

sentences.en: And the size of that gap didn't seem like a particularly meaningful decision until the bats moved in.
sentences.zh: 而这个间隙的大小似乎并不是一个特别重要的决定，直到蝙蝠搬进来。

sentences.en: Every year in the spring, Mexican free-tailed bats migrate from Mexico to central Texas,
sentences.zh: 每年春天，墨西哥无尾蝠从墨西哥迁徙到德克萨斯州中部，

sentences.en: and they're looking for caves or old barns or some other protected spot where they can safely hang upside down during the day.
sentences.zh: 它们寻找洞穴、旧谷仓或其他受保护的地点，以便白天可以在那里安全地倒挂着。

sentences.en: And shortly after the bridge renovation, a bunch of bats came across the new design and were like,
sentences.zh: 就在大桥翻新后不久，一群蝙蝠遇到了这个新设计，心想：

sentences.en: hey, this has got perfectly-sized cozy crevices now.
sentences.zh: 嘿，这里现在有了大小正合适的舒适缝隙。

sentences.en: It accidentally created this perfect environment for the bats to move into.
sentences.zh: 这无意中为蝙蝠搬进来创造了完美的环境。

sentences.en: In the years that followed the renovation, hundreds of thousands of free-tailed bats started roosting inside the bridge.
sentences.zh: 在翻新之后的几年里，几十万只无尾蝠开始在大桥内部筑巢。

sentences.en: And the people of Austin lost it.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀的人民彻底抓狂了。

sentences.en: There was quite a bit of hysteria in Austin back then about bats and rabies.
sentences.zh: 当时奥斯汀对蝙蝠和狂犬病存在相当多的歇斯底里。

sentences.en: The local newspaper, the Austin American Statesman, published headlines like,
sentences.zh: 当地报纸《奥斯汀美国政治家报》发表了这样的标题：

sentences.en: The New York Daily News went with,
sentences.zh: 《纽约每日新闻》则用了这样的标题：

sentences.en: Mass fear in the air as bats invade Austin.
sentences.zh: 随着蝙蝠入侵奥斯汀，恐慌弥漫空中。

sentences.en: And as the colony continued to grow, so did the fear.
sentences.zh: 随着蝙蝠群不断扩大，恐惧也在加剧。

sentences.en: Folks were starting to come up with plans to exterminate the bats, to get them out of the bridge,
sentences.zh: 人们开始想出各种计划来消灭蝙蝠，把它们赶出大桥，

sentences.en: because everybody knew that they were dangerous and a threat to human health and safety.
sentences.zh: 因为大家都知道它们很危险，对人类健康和安全构成了威胁。

sentences.en: The bats had just moved into their new home.
sentences.zh: 蝙蝠才刚刚搬进它们的新家。

sentences.en: And right away, it looked like they were about to get evicted, or even wiped out altogether.
sentences.zh: 紧接着，看起来它们就要被驱逐，甚至被彻底消灭了。

sentences.en: But someone was about to arrive in Austin to stick up for these bats,
sentences.zh: 但正要有人来到奥斯汀为这些蝙蝠挺身而出，

sentences.en: an advocate of sorts, in the court of public opinion.
sentences.zh: 算是在公众舆论法庭上的一个拥护者。

sentences.en: He was an ambitious young ecologist who was looking for a chance to show the world
sentences.zh: 他是一个雄心勃勃的年轻生态学家，正在寻找一个机会向世界证明，

sentences.en: not only that bats weren't as scary and dangerous as they were cracked up to be,
sentences.zh: 蝙蝠并不像人们想象的那样可怕和危险，

sentences.en: but that we could live harmoniously alongside them, right in the middle of a city.
sentences.zh: 而且我们完全可以与它们和谐共处，就在城市的正中央。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Merlin Tuttle, and I've studied bats for the last nearly 65 years.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是梅林·塔特尔，我研究蝙蝠已经快65年了。

sentences.en: Merlin Tuttle is one of the world's most prominent bat scientists.
sentences.zh: 梅林·塔特尔是世界上最著名的蝙蝠科学家之一。

sentences.en: And unlike a lot of people, he loves bats.
sentences.zh: 和很多人不同，他热爱蝙蝠。

sentences.en: He's been obsessed with them since he was a teenager, growing up in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 他从田纳西州长大的青少年时期起就对它们着迷了。

sentences.en: I lived just a couple miles from a bat cave, and became very fascinated with the bats.
sentences.zh: 我住的地方离一个蝙蝠洞只有几英里，变得非常迷恋蝙蝠。

sentences.en: I got so excited about bats that I forgot to go to school sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我对蝙蝠太兴奋了，有时甚至忘了去上学。

sentences.en: But he managed to get through high school and college, and eventually made it to graduate school.
sentences.zh: 但他设法读完了高中和大学，最终上了研究生。

sentences.en: research, he used to share bat caves with Tennessee moonshiners.
sentences.zh: 他曾经和田纳西州的私酒酿造者共享蝙蝠洞。

sentences.en: They even gave him his nickname.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至给他起了个绰号。

sentences.en: The moonshiners would actually yell across to each other,
sentences.zh: 私酒酿造者们甚至会大声朝彼此喊道：

sentences.en: They always had lookouts to make sure it wasn't the revenuers.
sentences.zh: 他们总是派放哨的人以确保来者不是税务官。

sentences.en: Merlin finished up his doctorate, and in 1975, he took a job in Wisconsin
sentences.zh: 梅林完成了博士学位，并在1975年接受了威斯康星州的一份工作，

sentences.en: as the curator of mammals at the Milwaukee Public Museum.
sentences.zh: 担任密尔沃基公共博物馆的哺乳动物馆长。

sentences.en: But it was kind of a tough time to be a bat scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个蝙蝠科学家，那是一个相当艰难的时期。

sentences.en: A public opinion poll had just shown that bats ranked just below rattlesnakes and cockroaches on public opinion.
sentences.zh: 一项民意调查刚刚显示，在公众心目中，蝙蝠的排名仅次于响尾蛇和小强。

sentences.en: Nearly everybody knew that most, if not all, bats were rabid and would attack you.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有人都知道，大多数（如果不是全部的话）蝙蝠都有狂犬病并且会攻击你。

sentences.en: Bats were seen as terrifying creatures of the night.
sentences.zh: 蝙蝠被视为可怕的暗夜生物。

sentences.en: Little furry monsters that would suck your blood and get tangled in your hair.
sentences.zh: 会吸血、会缠进你头发里的小毛怪。

sentences.en: And Merlin says he would regularly read articles in mainstream magazines
sentences.zh: 梅林说他经常在主流杂志上读到关于

sentences.en: about swarms of rabid bats attacking people.
sentences.zh: 成群患狂犬病的蝙蝠攻击人类的文章。

sentences.en: A lot of these stories bore no resemblance to reality.
sentences.zh: 许多这样的故事与现实毫无共同之处。

sentences.en: It is a fact that bats are involved in the majority of rabies cases in the United States,
sentences.zh: 事实是，蝙蝠确实参与了美国多数的狂犬病病例，

sentences.en: and that rabies is an extremely deadly disease.
sentences.zh: 并且狂犬病是一种极其致命的疾病。

sentences.en: But there are only one or two rabies cases a year in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 但美国每年只有一两起狂犬病例，

sentences.en: and it's not like those people were dive-bombed out of the blue by some bloodthirsty bat.
sentences.zh: 而且并不是说那些人被某种嗜血的蝙蝠无缘无故地俯冲轰炸了。

sentences.en: In all likelihood, they tried to pick up a bat, and they got bitten in self-defense.
sentences.zh: 很有可能，他们试图去抓蝙蝠，为了自卫才被咬的。

sentences.en: If they hadn't handled the bat, they'd have been perfectly safe.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不去抓蝙蝠，就会安然无恙。

sentences.en: Merlin insists that if we don't bother bats, they won't bother us.
sentences.zh: 梅林坚称，如果我们不打扰蝙蝠，它们就不会打扰我们。

sentences.en: And I mean, why would we bother bats?
sentences.zh: 再说，我们为什么要打扰蝙蝠呢？

sentences.en: They have social systems that are strikingly similar to those of higher primates.
sentences.zh: 它们的社会系统与高级灵长类动物惊人地相似。

sentences.en: They share information, they form long-term friendships, and they even adopt orphans.
sentences.zh: 它们分享信息，建立长期的友谊，甚至收养孤儿。

sentences.en: And they're also really important for humans.
sentences.zh: 而且它们对人类也非常重要。

sentences.en: They pollinate plants like mangoes and bananas.
sentences.zh: 它们给芒果和香蕉等植物传粉。

sentences.en: And all those agave plants from which the entire tequila and mezcal production comes,
sentences.zh: 所有生产龙舌兰酒和梅斯卡尔酒所需的龙舌兰植物，

sentences.en: are dependent on bats for pollination.
Without bats, you could lose a more than a billion-dollar industry.
sentences.zh: 如果没有蝙蝠，你可能会失去一个价值超过十亿美元的产业。

sentences.en: Bats also eat tons of bugs, including a lot of agricultural pests.
sentences.zh: 蝙蝠还吃掉大量的昆虫，包括许多农业害虫。

sentences.en: By some estimates, bats save U.S.
sentences.zh: 据一些估计，蝙蝠每年为美国农民节省了数

sentences.en: farmers billions of dollars every year in pest control.
sentences.zh: 十亿美元的害虫防治费用。

sentences.en: But in the 70s and 80s, as Merlin traveled the world doing his research,
sentences.zh: 但在70和80年代，当梅林环游世界进行研究时，

sentences.en: everywhere he went, he saw that bats were in trouble.
sentences.zh: 他走到哪里，都发现蝙蝠陷入了困境。

sentences.en: In that research, I couldn't help but notice that bat populations were declining at alarming rates.
sentences.zh: 在研究过程中，我忍不住注意到蝙蝠种群正在以惊人的速度下降。

sentences.en: Bats were losing habitat to logging and agriculture and being driven from their homes by cave explorers.
sentences.zh: 由于伐木和农业，蝙蝠正在失去栖息地，并被洞穴探险者赶出家园。

sentences.en: And in some places, people were just slaughtering them.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，人们甚至在大肆屠杀它们。

sentences.en: And as I saw that, I became more and more concerned at the rate at which people were killing these animals needlessly.
sentences.zh: 当我看到这些时，我对人们毫无必要地杀死这些动物的速度感到越来越担忧。

sentences.en: And so at a certain point, Merlin had an epiphany.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个时刻，梅林顿悟了。

sentences.en: He could spend his whole life studying bats, doing great science.
sentences.zh: 他可以花一辈子研究蝙蝠，做出伟大的科学成就。

sentences.en: But what good would it do if the animals that he loved were despised by everybody else?
sentences.zh: 但如果他热爱的动物被其他人唾弃，又有什么用呢？

sentences.en: He decided that he needed to get out of academia and devote himself to protecting these misunderstood creatures.
sentences.zh: 他决定离开学术界，全身心投入到保护这些被误解的生物中去。

sentences.en: Which a lot of smart people thought was a dumb idea.
sentences.zh: 许多聪明人认为这是一个愚蠢的主意。

sentences.en: Oh, my colleagues and even my best friends thought I was stark raving mad.
sentences.zh: 噢，我的同事甚至我最好的朋友都认为我简直疯了。

sentences.en: Bat conservation was viewed as a hopeless issue.
sentences.zh: 蝙蝠保护曾被视为一项无望的议题。

sentences.en: Even the world's biggest traditional conservation organizations wanted nothing to do with bats.
sentences.zh: 就连世界上最大的传统保护组织也对蝙蝠避之不及。

sentences.en: They were just deemed far too hopelessly unpopular to be helped.
sentences.zh: 它们被认为远远没有拯救的希望而不受欢迎。

sentences.en: In 1982, he launched an organization called Bat Conservation International, based in Milwaukee.
sentences.zh: 1982年，他在密尔沃基成立了一个名为“国际蝙蝠保护”的组织。

sentences.en: And he began touring the country preaching the bat gospel to anyone who would listen.
sentences.zh: 他开始在全国巡回演讲，向任何愿意听的人宣讲蝙蝠福音。

sentences.en: He has spent 20 years studying bats and feels that they don't get the respect they rightfully deserve.
sentences.zh: 他花20年时间研究蝙蝠，觉得它们没有得到应有的尊重。

sentences.en: Merlin did his best, but you can hear the audience squirming in their chairs when he starts pulling out live bats.
sentences.zh: 梅林尽了最大努力，但当他开始掏出活蝙蝠时，你能听到观众在座位上坐立不安。

sentences.en: And at times, it doesn't feel like Letterman is taking Merlin and his bats very seriously.
sentences.zh: 有时候，感觉莱特曼并没有把梅林和他的蝙蝠当回事。

sentences.en: What have you done to that chihuahua?
sentences.zh: 你对那只吉娃娃做了什么？

sentences.en: Merlin was facing an uphill battle, but in the mid-1980s, a major opportunity fell in his lap.
sentences.zh: 梅林面临着一场硬仗，但在20世纪80年代中期，一个重大机遇降临在他头上。

sentences.en: First time I heard about it, it was hundreds of thousands already.
sentences.zh: 我第一次听说的时候，就已经有几十万只了。

sentences.en: Merlin got word that a giant colony of free-tailed bats had moved into a bridge in Austin, Texas,
sentences.zh: 梅林接到消息称，一大群无尾蝠搬进了德克萨斯州奥斯汀的一座大桥，

sentences.en: and were causing a collective citywide freakout.
sentences.zh: 并引起了全城集体的恐慌。

sentences.en: We could send you a copy of a poster from the time that really tells the story,
sentences.zh: 我们可以给你寄一张当年的海报副本，上面真实地讲述了这个故事，

sentences.en: depicts everybody fleeing in terror and the bats coming out of the bridge.
sentences.zh: 描绘了所有人惊慌失措地逃跑，而蝙蝠从桥里飞出来的场景。

sentences.en: People were really frightened, and they were signing petitions to have the bats eradicated.
sentences.zh: 人们真的很害怕，他们正在签名请愿要求根除蝙蝠。

sentences.en: And I knew perfectly well that that was going to be the end of my efforts if I didn't do something about it.
sentences.zh: 我心里很清楚，如果我不采取行动，那将是我努力的终点。

sentences.en: And so in that moment, Merlin made a decision that would change the direction of his life
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时刻，梅林做了一个将改变他的人生方向

sentences.en: and the fate of the Austin colony.
sentences.zh: 以及奥斯汀蝙蝠群命运的决定。

sentences.en: He decided to pack up his things and move to Texas.
sentences.zh: 他决定收拾行囊搬到德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: Austin would be the new home of Bat Conservation International
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀将成为国际蝙蝠保护组织的新家，

sentences.en: and ground zero in Merlin Tuttle's public relations war on behalf of bats.
sentences.zh: 也是梅林·塔特尔代表蝙蝠发动公关战的中心战场。

sentences.en: One of the prettiest sites in Austin, Texas, is the Congress Street Bridge just before dusk.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州奥斯汀最美丽的景点之一是黄昏前的国会街桥。

sentences.en: What you would probably rather not see is underneath the bridge,
sentences.zh: 你可能最不想看到的场景是桥底下，

sentences.en: three-quarters of a million bats heading out for the night.
sentences.zh: 有七十五万只蝙蝠正准备外出过夜。

sentences.en: This newscast is from the late 80s, just after Merlin moved to town.
sentences.zh: 这段新闻广播来自80年代末，就在梅林搬到镇上之后。

sentences.en: For most of us, the mere thought of a bat conjures up notions of disease and disguSt.
sentences.zh: 对我们大多数人来说，仅仅想到蝙蝠就会联想到疾病和厌恶。

sentences.en: But that's wrong, according to Austin-based Bat Conservation International.
sentences.zh: 但根据总部位于奥斯汀的国际蝙蝠保护组织所说，这是不对的。

sentences.en: Merlin Tuttle and his staff claim bats have been getting a bad rap for centuries.
sentences.zh: 梅林·塔特尔和他的团队声称蝙蝠几个世纪以来一直背负着恶名。

sentences.en: They're vastly understudied, vastly underappreciated, and overly persecuted.
sentences.zh: 它们被严重低估、严重低估了价值，且遭受了过度的迫害。

sentences.en: But at first, Merlin's pro-bat message didn't go over too well in Austin.
sentences.zh: 但起初，梅林的亲蝙蝠信息在奥斯汀并不怎么受欢迎。

sentences.en: The magazine Texas Monthly gave Merlin their infamous Bumsteer Award,
sentences.zh: 《德克萨斯月刊》授予梅林他们臭名昭著的“笨蛋方向盘奖”，

sentences.en: a tongue-in-cheek honor typically reserved for corrupt politicians and other dubious figures.
sentences.zh: 这是一个带有讽刺意味的荣誉，通常留给腐败的政客和其他可疑人物。

sentences.en: And to be fair, at the time, the idea of saving bats did seem highly dubious.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，当时拯救蝙蝠的想法确实显得非常不靠谱。

sentences.en: You know, bats, as you know, have had a bad rap.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如你所知，蝙蝠一直名声不好。

sentences.en: This is Linda Moore, one of the first people Merlin hired after moving to Austin,
sentences.zh: 这是琳达·穆尔，梅林搬到奥斯汀后雇用的第一批人之一，

sentences.en: and one of his very first converts to Team Bat.
sentences.zh: 也是他最早的“蝙蝠战队”皈依者之一。

sentences.en: Linda responded to an ad for a bookkeeping job at a, quote, conservation organization.
sentences.zh: 琳达应聘了一家所谓“环保组织”的簿记员工作广告。
